- Fiscal policy and supply-side measures: Reducing budget deficits, improving productivity, removing supply bottlenecks.
- Inflation expectations: Central banks try to anchor expectations to prevent self-fulfilling wage-price spirals.

- 1970s U.S.: High inflation partly from oil shocks and expansive policies (stagflation with slow growth and high inflation).
- Weimar Germany (1920s) and Zimbabwe (2000s): Examples of hyperinflation.

  - Reinforcement learning (learn by trial and reward)

- Perception (e.g., computer vision, speech recognition)
